answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks with a slashable stake receipt. To join, an agent locks collateral on a public mesa anyone can audit, then gets a signed voucher from a randomly drawn peer panel. Each epoch vouchers are re-verified; forged ones burn the bond. Splitting into k fakes saves nothing: every puppet needs its own bond and honest attestor, so the attacker pays k times the capital with no compounding voice. A cedar voucher counts only with a real peer's signature, and the ferrous bond makes exit costly, so seizing influence costs more than the payoff.
